svg.title: Control ownership across four layers
svg.desc: Four owners in concentric responsibility. The image project owns verified inputs, a package-manager-free filesystem, a non-root default, reviewed configuration, and its own evidence. The deployment profile owns digest pinning, mounted material, runtime restrictions, limits, and probes. The host or orchestrator owns the kernel, isolation mechanisms, network policy, secrets, and log collection. The organization owns the control baseline, identities, monitoring, incident response, and authorization. A control the image contributes to is not a control the image satisfies.
svg.text: Control ownership
Contributing to a control is not satisfying it. Each layer depends on the ones outside it.
organization or system owner
control baseline and parameters · data classification · identities and separation of duties · central PKI,
logging and SIEM · incident response · continuous monitoring · exceptions · evidence retention · authorization
host or orchestrator
kernel and runtime patching · namespaces and cgroups · seccomp · SELinux · firewall and network policy
node identity · time synchronisation · journal and collector · secret service · admission policy · availability
deployment profile
pin the image by digest · mount configuration, content, trust material, and secrets read-only
set the read-only root, the tmpfs, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, and the assigned UID
choose the TLS mode · publish ports · define upstream, DNS, and egress policy · set resource limits
wire liveness and readiness probes correctly · own reload, rollback, and workload-specific tests
image project
verified, pinned inputs and hermetic assembly · package-manager-free filesystem · embedded inventory
non-root default identity · unprivileged listeners · no privilege transition at startup
reviewed configuration profiles with their tested boundaries · structured logging and its exclusions
scanner evidence, SBOM, requirement tree and trace matrix, decision records
the image can be configured insecurely by the layer above it, and cannot prevent that
No layer can discharge a control on behalf of another. A completed control matrix, system security plan, or authorization depends on the deployed boundary.
